concept: The site is graded by the roast you choose. One piece of state — where the drum stopped — is written by a photographic roast ladder and read by the nav chip, the ledger figures, the catalogue rack and the subscription shelf, so the whole page moves from green to dark with you.
recommendations: Keep the peak on the ladder: it is the only place where a click changes what the visitor can buy, so competing motion elsewhere would dilute it.
The brew guide is the post-peak development, not a second peak — its scroll scrub explains the real 30s/150s split rather than performing.
Reviews and the story stay still on purpose; they carry the concept through the roast ink and the ledger rules instead of motion.

sections.title: Roasted the morning it ships
sections.inputState: Cold load, no roast chosen yet; nav chip defaults to Medium.
sections.startState: Headline lines are clipped below their masks; the drum photograph sits at 1.0 scale under a heavy veil.
sections.endState: Three headline lines are revealed, the batch record card is visible, and by the end of the scroll the frame has drifted to 1.14 scale and darkened into the cut to paper.
sections.connection: Hands off to the ledger with a hard black-to-bone cut; the batch record's three numbers are the same three the ledger then sets in full size.
sections.desktop: Full-bleed roastery photograph with the headline set left over the dark side of the frame and the batch record card floating top right.
sections.mobile: Card leaves the image and becomes a three-column strip under the buttons; the veil flips to bottom-weighted so type never sits on the beans.
sections.reducedMotion: No line reveal and no scroll drift; the hero renders in its end state immediately.

sections.title: Still small on purpose
sections.inputState: Roast state as left by the ladder or its Medium default.
sections.startState: Paper surface, Probat photograph left, four figures ruled as a printed ledger.
sections.endState: Unchanged layout; the four figures and the section eyebrow carry the current roast ink.
sections.connection: Authored rest between the hero and the peak; it holds the concept through colour, not movement, and its rules are the same hairline system the catalogue uses.
sections.desktop: Two columns: a tall 4:5 machine photograph against a four-row figure ledger with oversized display numerals.
sections.mobile: Photograph capped at 420px and the ledger rows collapse to stacked figure-over-explanation.
sections.reducedMotion: Identical; the ink change is instant instead of eased.

sections.title: The roast ladder
sections.inputState: Medium, or whatever the visitor last pinned.
sections.startState: On first sight the ladder runs green to dark once and settles on Medium; the travelling brass indicator sits under rung 02.
sections.endState: The chosen rung is active, its macro photograph fills the stage, the readout names the drop point, and the page ink has changed to that roast.
sections.connection: This is the source of the shared state that the nav chip, story figures, catalogue rack and subscription shelf all read.
sections.desktop: 21:8 photographic stage with the readout over a directional scrim and a four-column rung strip beneath, joined by a travelling ink bar.
sections.mobile: Stage becomes 4:3, the readout note is dropped so the roast name and drop line stay legible, and the four rungs remain one horizontal ladder as tall tap targets.
sections.reducedMotion: The intro sequence is skipped entirely; selection is instant with no cross-fade.
sections.meaningfulOutcome: Choosing a rung opens that roast's coffees in the catalogue in full colour and changes which bags the subscription shelf lists.

sections.title: Six coffees, racked by roast
sections.inputState: The roast set by the ladder.
sections.startState: Three roast groups; two are racked as dense priced lines with duotoned thumbnails, one is open.
sections.endState: The selected group's coffees are dealt out as tall full-colour origin cards; the other two stay racked, priced and buyable.
sections.connection: Reads the ladder's state and turns it into the actual purchase decision; the group headings are also controls that write the state back.
sections.desktop: Rack of three groups; open group becomes an auto-fit card row with 4:5 origin photographs.
sections.mobile: Racked rows drop the photograph for a roast-ink tick, because a 52px landscape is a smudge; the open group becomes single-column 16:10 cards.
sections.reducedMotion: State changes apply with no transition; layout is identical.
sections.meaningfulOutcome: The visitor's roast preference decides which two or three coffees are shown at full size with origin, notes and price, without hiding the other four.

sections.title: The brew clock
sections.inputState: Arrives after the purchase decision; brew progress at 0.
sections.startState: The media panel is dry hatching, the axis fill is at zero and only the first step is lit.
sections.endState: The axis has filled to 3:00, the bloom photograph has given way to the pour photograph, and all four steps are lit with the last one current.
sections.mechanismOwner: gsap ScrollTrigger scrub + registered --brew custom property
sections.connection: Post-peak development: the same left-to-right ink bar the ladder uses, now measuring time instead of roast.
sections.desktop: Photographic band over a proportional time axis with a four-column step table beneath.
sections.mobile: Axis compresses and loses its sub-labels; steps stack full width and unreached steps dim rather than disappear.
sections.reducedMotion: Progress is pinned to 1 on mount, so the finished clock and the pour photograph are shown without scrubbing.
sections.meaningfulOutcome: The reader can see that two of the four steps happen before any water and that the bloom is a sixth of the brew, which the original four equal cards hid.

sections.title: Three subscribers
sections.startState: Three quotes stepped progressively further right on a ruled paper field.
sections.endState: Unchanged; the hanging quote marks carry the roast ink.
sections.connection: Deliberate quiet between the brew clock and the decision; the staircase indent is the only place the ledger rule system is broken on purpose.
sections.desktop: Full-width ruled rows with quote left and attribution right, each row indented further than the last.
sections.mobile: Indentation is removed and attribution moves under the quote.

sections.title: The shelf
sections.inputState: The roast chosen at the ladder.
sections.startState: The shelf panel lists the coffees of the current roast under an ink rule.
sections.endState: Changing the roast changes the named bags, their prices and the panel's rule colour.
sections.connection: The last stop for the shared state — the abstract roast choice becomes the concrete contents of a box.
sections.desktop: Pitch left, shelf panel right, both on iron.
sections.mobile: Panel drops below the pitch at full width.

sections.title: Two roasters read this
sections.startState: Email and message fields in a card topped by a roast-ink rule.
sections.endState: On submit the card is replaced by a stamped acknowledgement in the roast ink.
sections.connection: Closes the route on paper before the footer returns to iron with the roast stamp.
sections.desktop: Address column left, form card right.
sections.mobile: Stacked, inputs at 16px so iOS does not zoom.
sections.meaningfulOutcome: The preserved success state confirms the message was accepted and promises a reply within a day.
